_comment: The question Jev is asked per (claim, work) pair, by R/score_one_claim_jev.R.
Tracked as a format = 'file' target, so EDITING THIS FILE INVALIDATES SCORING.
Different question, different scores; a tree scored under two versions would be
meaningless. A real edit means a full rescore of whatever nli_config= uses the
jev backend.
A CHOICE, not three Nouls. The three labels are mutually exclusive, which is what
Choice is for -- the TypeSafe skill puts it as 'Choice: picks one option; its
distribution compares competing options' against 'Noul: ... use one per label when
several may apply'. Choice returns `probabilities` over the three labels and a
`confidence` directly, so (p_supports, p_refutes, p_nei) and confidence come back
native instead of being cross-normalised from three independent binaries. One
question per paper instead of three also means the premise is sent once.
The item goes in `instructions.paper`, NOT in the shared state. Question ids are
for code and are never sent to the model, so a question keyed by work_id against a
state full of papers has no way to say which paper it means -- measured: 40 papers
that way collapse to 3 distinct answers, and a paper plainly supporting a claim
scored 0.89 for CONTRADICTS. With the item inline, batch size has no measurable
effect: Spearman against per-paper scoring is 0.91 at 10 per request, 0.85 at 20,
0.88 at 40, against a 0.87 run-to-run baseline.
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO is the no-match outcome the skill calls for -- 'include a no-match
outcome when nothing may fit'. It must stay catch-all: a paper can fail to bear on
the claim either by being off-topic or by being on-topic and reporting nothing that
settles it, and both are NEI for this pipeline.

question.instructions_question: Judged only from this paper, what is its relationship to the claim?

criteria.SUPPORTS: the paper reports a finding consistent with the claim and bearing on it, making the claim more likely to be true
criteria.REFUTES: the paper reports a finding inconsistent with the claim, or pointing in the opposite direction, making the claim less likely to be true
criteria.NOT_ENOUGH_INFO: the paper does not report a finding that bears on the claim either way -- whether because it is about a related but different topic, or because it is on topic but reports nothing that settles the claim
